findings.title: Date override day skips all busy-time checks and returns available
findings.body: When any date override exists on the slot's day and the slot is not rejected by the override range check, `dateOverrideExist` is set and the function returns `true` at line 134 before reaching the `busy.every(...)` check. For a fixed host, a calendar event or existing booking overlapping the slot is ignored on any day that has a date override. This can allow double-booking, which is the opposite of what this PR is meant to fix.

findings.title: Working-hours check rejects slots if any single working-hours range does not cover them
findings.body: The `workingHours.find(...)` callback returns true for any working-hours entry where the slot falls outside it, and the `if` then rejects the slot when `find` finds any such entry. With several working-hours entries (multiple ranges on the same weekday, or entries for several users aggregated together), a slot covered by one entry is still rejected because another entry does not cover it. The check should ask whether no entry covers the slot, not whether some entry does not. Additionally, `start` and `end` at lines 141-142 are both computed from `slotStartTime`, so the end-of-slot is never checked against the working-hours end.

findings.title: Comparison of two dayjs objects with === is always false
findings.body: `dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...)` compares object references, not times, so the zero-length override branch (`return true`) can never execute. Zero-length overrides are therefore not handled as intended. Use `.isSame(...)` or compare `valueOf()`.

findings.title: Override timezone is optional but used unguarded, and the Date is round-tripped through a string
findings.body: `TimeRange.timeZone` is optional (packages/types/schedule.d.ts), and this PR now passes `availability.timeZone`, which may be undefined. `dayjs(...).tz(override.timeZone)` with an undefined zone falls back to the plugin default instead of failing clearly, so the offset can silently be wrong. Separately, `override.start.toString()` converts the Date to a locale-style string and re-parses it, which drops milliseconds and depends on the string format. Passing the Date (or its ISO string) directly and guarding the missing timezone would be safer.

findings.title: Timezone test does not exercise round-robin or fixed-host overrides
findings.body: The added assertion only checks a personal event with one host and expects the same UTC slots for a +6:00 invitee as for +5:30. It does not cover the bug the PR fixes: a round-robin event with a fixed host whose date override limits slots, nor the busy-time bypass described above. No test covers the case where a calendar busy time on an override day should still block a slot, so the regression in the override early return would go undetected.
